## Why

`entire repo mirror list` only showed existing mirrors; the repos you *could* mirror were hidden behind a separate `--show-available` mode, with its own endpoint and its own table shape. `GET /repos?scope=all` returns existing mirrors and onboardable GitHub candidates in one discriminated shape — so the list can just show both, and the per-cluster detail moves to a proper `get` view.

## What

### One list: mirrored and mirrorable repos

`entire repo mirror list` renders one table, one row per repo, from a single `/repos?scope=all` call:

```
NAME (owner/repo)   CLUSTERS                            VISIBILITY  STATUS     ACCESS
entirehq/entiredb   aws-us-east-2, aws-eu-central-1     Private     ready      -
acme/marketing      -                                   Public      available  admin
```

- **Mirrors** — one row per repo (not per placement, so a four-cluster repo no longer occupies four rows). CLUSTERS lists the placement slugs; STATUS is the placements' shared clone status (`ready`/`processing`/`failed`/`suspended`) or `mixed` when they disagree. A placement on a cluster the catalog can't resolve still names its slug (no clone URL is fabricated for it).
- **Candidates (repos that can be mirrored)** — ACCESS + an `available`/`owner-only` STATUS; no clusters.
- `--mirrored` / `--available` (mutually exclusive) keep one row type: existing mirrors, or onboardable candidates (owner-only included). The old `--show-available` flag is removed.
- Colored like `trail list`, TTY only (pipes, `--json`, `NO_COLOR` see bare text): yellow headers, cyan clusters/access, visibility by audience (Public green, Private magenta), status by lifecycle (ready/available green, processing/mixed yellow, failed red, suspended magenta).
- `--json` emits the directory rows with nested `placements: [{cluster, status, cloneUrl}]`; the raw wire model stays at `entire api --to core /repos`.
- Truncated results warn on stderr (the endpoint has no pagination cursor). **Native (non-mirror) placements are dropped** — a repo created by `entire repo create` has no GitHub mirror clone URL to advertise.

Every displayed column is sortable and filterable (client-side, before render):

| Column | `--sort` key | Filter |
|---|---|---|
| NAME (owner/repo) | `name` | `--name` (substring), `--owner` |
| CLUSTERS | `clusters` | `--cluster` (slug **or** public host, matching any placement) |
| VISIBILITY | `visibility` | `--private` (tri-state) |
| STATUS | `status` | `--status` (exact; matches any placement, so `--status failed` surfaces a repo whose cell reads `mixed`) |
| ACCESS | `access` | `--access` (exact; candidates only) |

`--sort` takes a `-` prefix for descending; default is name ascending with a deterministic name+clusters tiebreak.

### Per-cluster detail: `mirror get <owner/repo>`

`entire repo mirror get` now also accepts the NAME cell verbatim (ULID and clone-URL forms unchanged) and renders a record — the clone URLs are the payload:

```
Name:
  entirehq/entiredb
Visibility:
  Private

CLUSTER             CLONE URL                                                  STATUS
aws-eu-central-1    entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/entirehq/entiredb   ready
aws-us-east-2       entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/gh/entirehq/entiredb      ready
```

One exact-match `/repos?filter=` lookup, no directory walk. `--json` emits the same nested-placements row shape as `list --json`. An Access section renders when the server provides it (candidate entries); a candidate renders its availability instead of a placements table, ready for when the control plane's filter starts matching onboardable repos — today it matches onboarded only, so the not-found error points at `list --available`.

The list footer hints the drill-down on stderr (skipped for `--json` and empty tables):

```
Per-cluster detail and clone URLs: entire repo mirror get <owner/repo>
```

Placements carry only a cluster slug, so clone URLs are reconstructed by joining the slug against the cluster catalog (`ListClusters`).

## Depends on

Stacks on the coreapi schema regen + caller adaptations + cell fan-out fix, split out to **#1694** (merged to `main`).

## Test plan

- `go build ./...`, golangci-lint v2 (0 issues), full `cmd/entire/cli` package green, `mise run test:ci` (unit + integration + Vogon canary) green.
- List: merged-list routing, grouping (multi-placement single row, mixed-status roll-up, native-drop, unresolvable-slug), all filters + sort (`--mirrored`/`--available` split + mutual exclusion, any-placement `--cluster`/`--status`, tri-state `--private`, tiebreaks, case-insensitivity), fetch budget/pagination, truncated warnings, detail-hint gating, plain output on non-TTY (color gate).
- Get: owner/repo record view (exact-match filter routing, per-cluster table order, candidate rendering, `--json` row shape, not-found error), ULID/clone-URL routing unchanged.
- Verified live against the control plane: grouped list, type filters, and the `mirror get entirehq/entiredb` record across four clusters, colors under a PTY and bare text when piped.

## Review: PR #1681 — one `repo mirror list` for mirrored + mirrorable repos

**Verdict: strong. Approve with one cosmetic regression to note + minor nits.** +2422/−529, 10 files. Tests exceptional — grouping, mixed-status roll-up, native-drop, unresolvable-slug, every filter/sort, fetch budget, page mode, truncation disclosure, host-spoof guard. CI green per PR body.

### What it does
- Collapses `mirror list` (existing) + `--show-available` (onboardable) into one `/repos?scope=all` table, one row per repo (was one per placement). Adds `mirror get <owner/repo>` record view.
- Adds shared list infra: bounded fetch walk (`fetchPagesBounded` + 1000 budget), single-page cursor passthrough (`--page-size/--page-token`), grouped flag help, pager wrapping.
- Removes `--show-available` and `--provider`.

### Finding 1 — `repo list` loses table color on a TTY (regression) `repo.go`
`newRepoListCmd` now wraps render in `flushThroughPager`, which swaps stdout for a `bytes.Buffer`. `printTable` calls `newTableStyles(w)` → `shouldUseColor(buffer)` → **false**, so the primary/secondary column styling is dropped even on an interactive terminal.

`mirror list` dodges this by pre-coloring cells against the *real* writer before the swap (`repoDirCellsStyled`/`styledHeaders`) — `repo list` does **not** pre-color, so its output silently goes from colored → plain.
- Impact: cosmetic only; alignment and content unaffected (buffer path leaves the pre-plain text intact). No test covers repo-list color, so it changed silently.
- Fix options: pre-style `repo list` the same way, or have `flushThroughPager` carry the origin writer's color decision into the render. Low severity — flag, your call whether to fix here.

### Finding 2 — `--provider` removal undocumented `repo_mirror.go:1382`
`--show-available` removal is called out in the PR body; the `--provider` flag drop isn't. Both are user-facing flag removals. Worth a line in the PR "What" for the changelog.

### Nits (non-blocking)
- `renderRepoDetail:1552` reimplements `printTable`'s width+row loop (`columnWidths`/`writeTableRow` with a `plain` styleFor) to keep pre-colored cells intact. Justified by the pre-color constraint, but it's a third table renderer — a shared "render pre-styled table" helper would DRY `repoDirCellsStyled`, `styledHeaders`, and this.
- Candidate wording `renderRepoDetail`: `"Not mirrored on any cluster (available)."` reads oddly — `available` means *available to onboard*, not a mirror state. Minor.
- mirror-list `--limit N` on a huge dir still prints `"first 1000 fetched"` on stderr even though only N rows show. Correct (window vs cap are distinct) but potentially confusing. Fine as-is.

- **Ref routing** `get`: ULID → `isOwnerRepoRef` → clone-URL, correctly ordered; `isOwnerRepoRef` rejects `://`, multi-segment, empty sides (`TestIsOwnerRepoRef` covers).
- **Host-spoof guard**: `clusterHostBySlug` drops userinfo-smuggling publicUrls → dashed clone URL, never spoofed. Tested (`host@evil.com`).

## What changed

**Bug:** `repo list` now wraps its render in `flushThroughPager`, which swaps stdout for an in-memory buffer. `printTable` decides color from the writer it renders into — a buffer is never a TTY — so `repo list` lost its table color on interactive terminals. `mirror list` dodged this by pre-styling; `repo list` did not.

**Fix** (`corecmd.go`, `repo.go`):
- Added `preStyleTable` (+ pure `styleTableWith` core) — colors headers and routes each cell through its column style against the **real** output writer, before the buffer swap. The buffered render's own color gate is off, so it passes the ANSI through without re-styling. Identity when color is off → pipes/tests/`NO_COLOR` stay byte-for-byte plain.
- `newRepoListCmd` computes `headers, row := preStyleTable(cmd.OutOrStdout(), …)` once and feeds both the walk and page-mode render paths.

**Test** (`corecmd_test.go`): `TestStyleTableWith` pins both paths — enabled colors headers + splits primary/secondary columns (same split `printTable` uses); disabled is an exact identity.

## Verification
- `go build ./cmd/...` — clean
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/` — ok (38s, full package)
- golangci-lint v2.11.3 (direct binary, per the v1-shadow issue) — **0 issues**

`mise run lint` still fails locally from the stale golangci-lint v1 on the go bin PATH — not related to this change.

Note: the color-**on** path can't be exercised end-to-end in `go test` (no real TTY), matching the existing `TestStyledCellsDisabledGate` convention; `TestStyleTableWith` covers it at the unit level via an injected enabled `tableStyles`.
